learning_outcomes.text: Develop mathematical models of electromechanical systems, primarily power converters and electrical machines for their application in control.
Analyze, design, and simulate control systems for power converters.
Analyze, design, and simulate control systems for electromechanical systems.
Program and implement digital controllers for electromechanical systems.
Select and parameterize industrial power converters.

syllabus_topics: Scalar control of the induction motor
Description of industrial drives and commercial motion control systems
Selection and application of industrial drives and commercial motion control systems

assessment_methods.method: Exercises, assignments, and presentations developed during the course

assessment_rules: The final grade (N) is calculated as 0.7 * T + 0.3 * P, where T is the theoretical block grade and P is the practical block grade. A minimum grade of 5/10 is required for the theoretical block and 4/10 for the practical block to pass the course. If these minimums are not met, the maximum grade awarded will be 4. For extraordinary exams, the same criteria apply, with a practical lab exam for students who haven't completed the practical part. Students under the differentiated assessment regime will take a single theoretical-practical exam and must obtain a minimum of 5/10 to pass.
